_note: House rules earned the hard way. Matched by keyword against any future shot's beat/prompt so a lesson is paid for once, ever.

lessons.lesson: a beat used to judge a CLIP must be judgeable from a single frame — describe a STATE, not a change over time. 'the crack of light widens' and 'she steps down out of the doorway' were rejected on every probe because no single frame can show a change.

identity drifts hardest when a character is SMALL in frame — wide shots came back with a smaller head and lighter orange fur and failed the identity gate. Frame characters large enough to read on-model, or build the wide as a plate and place characters via crops/inserts.

a diffusion model draws 'circus train' as a happy train rolling along. To read as trouble it must be described as STOPPED DEAD and in distress with no motion cues at all — cold, stranded, crooked on the rails, smoke pouring up.

NEVER prompt an impact or collision. Wan converts 'splinters bursting' into a continuous particle spray that reads as drilling. Render the effort, and let the bang be felt from elsewhere — dust, shudder, a widening light crack.

batch a queue BY MODEL, not by shot — all stills first, then all animations. Alternating mflux and Wan GGUF per shot pushes the box into swap and the memory gate bounces ComfyUI (~90s, six times in one hour = ~15% of wall clock).

a beat is a VISIBLE STATE. No intent ('trying to reach'), no offscreen facts ('the frightened animal inside'), no change over time ('the door widens'). Anything a viewer with no script cannot see in one frame will fail every probe and the fault is the spec, not the judge.

identity questions must allow for scale, distance, lighting and angle. Comparing a close portrait master to a wide shot literally makes every wide 'drift' — ask about DESIGN (species, build, head/ear shape, colour scheme, art style), never about apparent size or warmth.

audit the auditor: keep a calibration set of shots with KNOWN human verdicts and re-run it whenever wording changes. First run agreed 5/6; the single disagreement was a badly worded beat. A gate that disagrees with the human under 80% of the time is not strict, it is broken.

majority voting is load-bearing, not a nicety: two shots Matt approved scored 2/3 with one pedantic dissent ('the stick is not a fishing rod'). Single-frame judging would have rejected work he had already accepted.

the local-AI videos that actually earn thousands of upvotes use MANY steps (up to 60) and finish at high resolution with ZERO film grain — grain is how people hide smeared texture after upscaling. 24 steps at 832x480 is a draft, not a finish.

what earns upvotes is CONSISTENCY across a whole scene, not one pretty clip — the 2.6k-upvote local anime post chained image-to-video off the last frame to reach 30-second continuous scenes with the same characters.

FLUX.2 accepts NO negative prompt and treats 'NO animals/people' in a positive prompt as an instruction to draw them. To get an empty plate, describe it positively — deserted, abandoned, silent, not a soul in sight — and let the gate's must_not do the rejecting.

LOCK THE SET, not just the characters. The door Hank pushes and the door that opens were different cars entirely — sliding wooden panel on a plain red car vs double hinged doors on a yellow-banded car in a different landscape. beat_gate supports set_masters and this film never armed it. Any shot sharing a location declares its set and is checked against the locked plate.

Never put a word in CAPITAL LETTERS in an image prompt — the model renders capitalised words as literal painted signage. 'boxcars with SHUT doors' put the word SHUT in yellow capitals across two train cars. Use lower case, and add 'no lettering or writing anywhere' for vehicles.

A beat must name PHYSICAL VISIBLE facts. A single frame cannot show absence-of-motion ('stopped') or an internal state ('clearly worried') — both failed every ballot until restated. If independent runs fail with the SAME words, the beat is wrong, not the roll: stop re-rolling.

A set-continuity master only works against shots at COMPARABLE SCALE. One master cannot serve both: a door close-up flunks every wide shot, a wide establishing view flunks every close-up. Keep a wide master and a detail master, and have each shot name the one at its scale.

A gate that writes the WRONG lesson is worse than no gate. Distinct rejection reasons must stay distinct — text-in-frame recorded as identity DRIFT taught 'draw the character on-model and larger', a correction unrelated to the defect, saved permanently and carried into later films.

i2v dies silently with NO crash log when jetsam SIGKILLs it, while memory_pressure reports 93% free — the nearly-full swap file is what runs out, and nothing measures it. Bounce ComfyUI immediately before every animate, and reclaim on BOTH sides of the render, not just before.

Gates judge ASSETS; nothing judges the POINTER. An EDL entry aimed at the wrong file gets a truthful verdict to the wrong question. Cross-check EDL ids against beats.json by id before any model loads — it is a string compare.

never describe Doug as lanky, slim or long-legged in any prompt — he is a STURDY bloodhound (deep chest, heavy build, long dark ears past the jaw, droopy eyes); prompt adjectives override the LoRA and produce a skinny off-model dog (Matt rejected it 2026-07-31)

NEVER prompt physical contact between two characters — a paw under a chin, a hug, a handshake. Wan fuses the touching limbs into a mangled lump (rule 6). Stage characters with clear air between them; warmth comes from posture, gaze and light, not touch.

A process killed while holding a forge_guard lease keeps the lease until its TTL (film_qc: 1h). Every later ask that would exceed the 50GB non-forge budget then silently waits the full 900s timeout and only THEN proceeds. Three renders and one QC lost 15 minutes each on 2026-08-29. Before diagnosing a 'stuck' judge or render: `python3 ~/SongForgeM5/mem_client.py state` → release orphan leases. Ask for what the job really needs (≤20GB with --low-ram).

Scene i2v: LTX-2.5 distilled --low-ram ≈ 70s per 5s clip vs Wan 13–16 min, same composition held. Dialogue a2v: keep mlx-video LTX-2 distilled (42s) — ltx-2-mlx a2v is dev+CFG and takes 4+ min with a swap spike. Numbers in RENDER_SPEED_RESEARCH.md 2026-08-29.

LTX-2.5 i2v adds push-ins, pans and pull-backs on its own; a clip then fails a beat the still passed (s1_coldopen 3 fails, s4_arrival 2 fails). 'Static camera, locked-off tripod shot, the camera does not move at all and the framing never changes from the first frame' held the frame; make-ltx25 now prepends it to every i2v prompt that does not ask for a move.

The rollout shipped with the horse BEHIND the wagon it pulls (Matt: 'the wagon is pulling the horse, it makes no sense'). Three failures stacked: (1) the beat gate only asks 'does this depict the beat' — a horse + wagon + dust is a PASS with no physics check; (2) the trim rule kept a 2s window (t=3.5–4.5s) that passed the same question while the full clip failed 1/5; (3) nobody looked at KEPT clips — only failed ones got eyeballed. Fixes: HOUSE_MUST_NOT in beat_gate fails impossible geometry on every ballot; a pulling shot must state the geometry in beat AND must_not ('horses out in front, wagon behind them'); and every kept clip gets a frame-grid look by the agent before assembly.

Second rollout failure the same morning, AFTER HOUSE_MUST_NOT shipped: both wagon shots came back as a CONVOY (a horse's rump at frame left, two loose horses charging at camera behind the wagon) and the judge passed the clips 5/5. Causes: (1) the init plate wagon_canon.png is a REAR three-quarter view, so from that angle a horse in front of the wagon is hidden by the wagon body and the model invents horses elsewhere; (2) the stored prescribe() lessons said 'add a galloping horse in the foreground on the left' — written for that plate, they kept manufacturing the rump; (3) a VL judge cannot be trusted on who-pulls-whom geometry even when told the rule. Fixes: any shot where one thing pulls another is staged in clean SIDE PROFILE or a low three-quarter FRONT view with no init plate, the prompt says 'a single wagon, the only vehicle on the road', must_not forbids a second wagon/convoy, loose horses, head-on horses, a horse cut by the frame edge and a rear end in the foreground; retire prescriptions when the staging changes; and every kept clip is eyeballed at full frame at 4+ timestamps before it goes near the cut.

Matt caught a THREE-headed pair of horses in the first frame of the rebuilt rollout after the agent had looked at it and called it right ('two-to-three horses' was written down and waved through). Any shot with two or more of the same animal side by side: count heads, count bodies, count legs — they must match — and put 'three or more heads / more heads than bodies / animals merged into each other' in must_not. Give a pair different coats so the model keeps them separate. A defect the reviewer can name in words and still ships is worse than one never seen.

A clip_beat must describe what ONE frame shows at any moment of the motion, never the CHANGE itself. 's6c: the seam of light steadily WIDENING' failed 0/5 on a clip that widened perfectly, because each sampled frame was judged alone and no single frame depicts 'widening'. Write clip_beats as a state true of every frame (e.g. 'light pouring through a partly or fully open doorway'), and let a human confirm the motion.

never put a MOTION or STATE-CHANGE claim in a beat used to judge a STILL — the judge infers motion from smoke shape and leg pose and fails BOTH directions ('smoke plume is dynamic so the train is moving' killed 'stopped train'; 'legs not blurred so not rolling' killed 'wagon rolling away'; 'steaming so not repaired' killed 'repaired train'). State only what pixels can prove: doors shut, smoke pouring, horses out front, dust behind the wheels.

emotion and vibe words in a beat or clip_beat make the judge rule on mood it cannot verify — 'celebrating/joyfully' failed a frame that showed every required animal present. Name observable cues (ears swaying, head tipped back, mouth open) or drop the word.

one clip per beat is not a film: shoot >= 3 setups per line from >= 2 sources (acquired seconds >= 3x runtime), keep alternates in acquired/ and clips/alternates/ listed in manifest.json until the FILM is approved, rank >= 2 takes per line in selects.json, and cut to the best. coverage_gate.py blocks the edit until this holds (frozen rules 13 amended, 29).

drift is not motion: 'gentle ambient motion, subtle camera push-in' and a forced 'static camera, locked-off' prefix gave every shot the same nothing, and Matt rejected that look three times. Name the subject's action and a camera move chosen for THIS shot (push in as the realization lands, track alongside the walk, pull back to reveal); static is an explicit --static / "static": true choice (frozen rule 31).

narration laid over a run of clips with a 0.5 s crossfade at every join reads as a slideshow. Align the VO to words (words_align.py), pick cue words per line (cues.json), hard-cut on word onsets, and dissolve only where a cue says xfade (frozen rule 32).

QC that checks faces never notices a product drawn wrong (an extra leg, a motor in the wrong place). Every product shot is checked against design.json (reference angles, counted facts, must_not) by design_check.py before it can be selected (RULES.md 29).

ChatGPT images and Grok Imagine video are allowed ONLY via bin/browser-acquire in Matt's Brave on the mini (hidden lease tabs, never focus-stealing, never an API), each take with a provenance sidecar, and they pass every gate including design_check. Grok free tier = 480p and 6 s; never click the upsell (frozen rule 28).

never show Matt a cut the agent has not watched start to finish: all gate reports read, then known_defects.md dated, confirming the full watch, newer than the newest final/*.mp4. bin/film-status prints READY FOR MATT: no until then (frozen rule 30).

scripts were written for the VL judge, not the viewer, and no spec ever said what the viewer should feel. Every line/beat carries a SENTIMENT line; write the story for the viewer, then stage the shot so the judge can verify it, never the other way round (RULES.md 32).

a browser generation that does not look like OUR design is a wrong shot, however pretty (Matt was upset by one). Every browser-acquire job uploads CAD stills of the matching pose/angle as refs, best match FIRST (Grok animates from the first ref only), and every prompt carries the design.json fidelity_clause telling the tool to reproduce that exact design, photoreal. browser-acquire refuses empty refs (frozen rule 28).

a voice line is only usable once whisper hears every word of it AFTER the finish chain: the pitch shift turned 'camp chair' into 'cam chair' (Sitka) and 'This is Sitka' into 'to Sitka' three takes running (sitka_demo). promo_voice.py retakes, then auto-rewords (alt: lines, numbers as words, the misheard word set off by commas), and every later gate checks what was SPOKEN.

an HDRI world with only a shadow catcher left the product floating over the photo's far-away ground (sitka_demo l02, struts in the air). HDRI shots get a real rough ground under the product that fades to transparent at ~3x its size; studio shots get a dark sweep that fades to black so no horizon line shows.

the end-card slam (flash + hit + the bed's downbeat + the sting) lands AFTER the last word ends (slam_after 0.15 s), never on it: on Sitka the hit masked 'Come'. edit_to_words stops the shots at the slam, promo_mix offsets the bed's downbeat onto it, cue_check and promo_gates fail a slam that starts before the last heard word ends.

never run a live browser generation to test a tool: bin/browser-acquire --mock runs the same validation, prompt building, numbering, sidecars and provenance with no browser and no mini, and its fake takes go to acquired/_mock/, which ingest never reads.

before writing any production plan, list the model weights actually on disk (du the real files, not the cache folder names): on 10/31 the plan named Wan 2.2 and Flux, both deleted on 10/25, and the Qwen-Image cache entry was 4 KB. Plan only with what is there.

never give a finish time before the first clip is timed. Measured on the M5 10/31: LTX-2.5 --hq --low-ram at 832x480 ~9-10 min per ~3.5 s take (~160 s per second of footage); LTX previs ~106 s per 5 s clip; Blender Cycles ship stills 11-41 s, volumetric 6 min, animation ~12 s/frame at 48 samples.

check the memory guard's free allowance BEFORE the image phase and pick a model that fits: on 10/31 Qwen-Image needed 48 GB, the guard allowed 23 because of another job, and the phase stalled 16 min until Z-Image-Turbo (bf16, fits) took over.
LTX shots on this film degraded into haze/darkness after 2-3.5 s: render each shot at the cut length plus ~0.5 s handles, never a blanket 5 s (baked into 04_shots step 5).
a gated download is never a reason to ask Matt to sign in: swap to a model already on disk (Stable Audio Open was HF-gated, MMAudio already local and Matt approved its rumble by ear).

SeedVR2-3B fp16 on the M5 (torch MPS) runs ~13 s per OUTPUT frame at 720p short side; the VAE decode is ~70% of it, VAE tiling does not speed it up, and 4K direct is ~6x slower (7 min just to encode 21 frames). Budget the upscale before promising 4K: SeedVR2 only the held shots (>= ~0.9 s) to ~2x, lanczos to 4K, and lanczos the sub-second cuts.

the SeedVR2 node CLI stubs a fake flash_attn module on Macs; newer transformers then dies with KeyError 'flash_attn'. Launch it through projects/last_signal/tools/seedvr2_run.py, which imports transformers' flash-attention probe before the stub exists.

the VL clip gate failed 34 of 44 good takes because clip_beats said motion ('rushes toward', 'keeps rising', 'for the whole shot') and the judge reads each sampled frame as 'static'. Write clip_beats as what ONE frame can show at any point of the shot (the ship large in frame with streaking rocks, the giant towering over the monoliths), never a verb of motion.

when a mix plan clamps sources out of a silence window (dead stop, black), never clamp the full-length timeline tracks (score, beep, sub hits): the first pass cut the score at the dead stop and the whole ramp went near-silent. Check per-half-second RMS of every render against the beat map before calling a mix done.

MMAudio text-mode 'long riser' came back as white-noise hiss (spectral flatness 0.45, centroid 10.7 kHz). Measure flatness + centroid of every generated SFX and drop anything noise-like before it reaches the mix.
an 'until ! pgrep -f PATTERN' waiter matches its OWN command line and never exits; wait on the job's PID or its log file instead.

SeedVR2 CLI on MPS: in a run with THREE temporal batches the middle batch came back grey with white smears, twice (batch 45 and 41, seeds unchanged); 1- and 2-batch runs were clean. Keep every run to <= 2 batches (split long shots into chunks of one batch each) and compare every output frame to its source at thumbnail size before using it (tools/seedvr2_batch.py bad_frames).
